name: Wales
summary: A red dragon passant on a field of white over green. The dragon has been a Welsh symbol since at least the early Middle Ages; the white and green were the colours of the House of Tudor.
origin: The red dragon appears in the 9th-century 'Historia Brittonum', in the legend of a red dragon (the Britons) defeating a white dragon (the Saxons). Henry Tudor, of Welsh descent, carried a red dragon on green and white at the Battle of Bosworth in 1485.
The flag was officially recognised as the flag of Wales by Queen Elizabeth II in 1959. Wales is not represented on the Union Flag because it was annexed to England before the union with Scotland.
